title: Install Google Analytics through Google Tag Manager

history.detail:
PASS: PASS, gate 1, audit of 2a74097.

Sprint file: read fresh at this commit (status in_progress, created 22:07:51). The handoff was read at the audited commit with git show 2a74097:docs/handoffs/sprint-46.md. It has a Round 1 section that quotes VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0, with 45 files and 511 tests.

My own check: npm run verify at 2a74097, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS exit=0, 45 test files and 511 tests passed.

Requirements:
- R1 Met. app/layout.tsx renders TagManager once, inside body. grep finds TagManager or googletagmanager only in app/TagManager.tsx, app/layout.tsx, lib/analytics/tag-manager.ts and their tests. No page renders it.
- R2 Met. Google's snippet verbatim, through next/script: the inline half is beforeInteractive, the container is afterInteractive. A test pins the text exactly. Next 16's own docs (02-components/script.md:75) require beforeInteractive in the root layout, and TagManager is rendered only from there. The no-new-dependency choice over @next/third-parties is justified in the handoff. grep -rnE for G- IDs or gtag/js over app and lib exits 0, but the only hit is the test comment at tag-manager.test.ts:21. No measurement ID is in the code; G-NFY3Q9KSXH appears only in the handoff evidence, as what the container itself sent.
- R3 Met. shouldLoadTagManager is a strict equality check for production. TagManager has no use client, so it's a server component, and it returns null otherwise. grep for NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV across source exits 1. Production deploys through the CI deploy hook, so Vercel builds and runs with VERCEL_ENV=production. The GitHub Actions test job doesn't set VERCEL_ENV, so the test asserting it's unset holds in CI.
- R4 Met. GTM-T9WQSKH3 appears once outside tests, at lib/analytics/tag-manager.ts:7 (grep exit 0, one line). A broader GTM- pattern gives the same single hit.
- R5 Met. Outside new files, only app/layout.tsx changed. The reworded font comment is accurate.
- R6 Met. Tests cover production, preview, development, unset, empty and wrong-case values, the real process.env path via vi.stubEnv, and the exact ID and URL.
- R7 Met. The README Analytics section covers the ID, that only production loads it, and that GA4 is configured in Tag Manager, with a double-count warning and the history-change note.
- R8 Met. No new dependency.

Dev Team's question 1, the 500 error shell: ACCEPTABLE, not a defect under R2. Next serves the bare error document with the root layout rendered only on the client, so no server-rendered beforeInteractive is possible there with any of R2's allowed approaches. The container still ran once, and GTM creates dataLayer itself. R2's dataLayer-first holds on every page the layout server-renders, which is every page R1 names. Master Controller may record this ruling in the sprint file if wanted. It does not need a code change.

Evidence files: I checked docs/handoffs/sprint-46 for keys (eyJ, service_role) and found none (exit 1).

Notes for the user and LiveQA:
- The 4 real GA4 hits from Dev Team's first local probe (127.0.0.1 and localhost hostnames) are in the stream. The user may want to filter or ignore them. This is informational, not a blocker.
- Dev Team's local production build already saw the container send a page_view, so the GA4 tag looks configured. Per the handoff, in-app navigation sent no second page_view, which matches the sprint's own Human Prerequisite on history-change page views. LiveQA records step 4 either way.

No issues found. Nothing new for Human Prerequisites beyond those already in the sprint file.
commit=2a74097 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 2a7409741549b913fc3139d37da6b487a46768b2 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL (round 1). One defect, against R1.
The defect: route-level 404s, where /date/[date] or /reading/[id] call notFound(), request the container gtm.js TWICE, and their visit is never counted in GA4 (no page_view).
- Normal pages, in-app navigation, the plain unknown-path 404 and the production-only switch all pass.
- Steps 1 to 6 were run. Step 7 (GA4 Realtime) was not checked: nobody was watching Analytics during the test.

Tested 2026-11-24, about 22:45 to 23:05 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 2a74097. Production serves the pushed tip 6323e48: /api/health/db reports status ok, connected true, commit 6323e48, with migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff --stat 2a74097 origin/main touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-46.json.
Tools:
- Headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1280x1000, with a fresh context per page, and CDP Network.requestWillBeSent to record each request's initiator.
- curl.
- A fresh git clone at 2a74097 in a scratch directory: npm ci exit=0 and npm run build exit=0 (no VERCEL_* variables in the shell), then next start.
Note: my production runs sent real GA4 hits to G-NFY3Q9KSXH, on hostname my-little-racoon.vercel.app, around 22:45 to 23:00 UTC, from headless Chromium. No local run executed the tag, so no localhost hits came from this test.

DEFECT: route-level 404s load the container twice, and send no page_view.
Pages: /date/not-a-date, /date/1054-07-04 and /reading/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000. All three return 404, with title "404: This page could not be found.". In each, with a fresh context:
- gtm.js?id=GTM-T9WQSKH3 is requested 2 times. CDP shows both as type Script, initiator=script, from two different Next client chunks: .../chunks/357s7nr6pq7in.js and .../chunks/3aa4fr35vqpis.js. A normal page requests it once, initiator=parser, from the page HTML.
- 0 g/collect hits are sent, even after waiting and then navigating away to about:blank to flush. By contrast, /no-such-page (also a 404) sends page_view@/no-such-page.
- The dataLayer starts with an empty first entry ([]), and its events are only gtm.dom, gtm.load and gtm.scrollDepth. There is no "js" command and no gtm.js event, so the container's All Pages trigger never fires. On normal pages, dataLayer[0] is ["js", <timestamp>].
- The server HTML has GTM-T9WQSKH3 once and window.dataLayer once, against twice each on normal pages. There is no inline snippet in <head> (the inline scripts are BODY,BODY only), so both are injected client-side.
- I reproduced this on my local production build with VERCEL_ENV=production: /date/not-a-date's server HTML has 1 occurrence of each, against 2 on /date/1969-07-20. So it comes from the code, not from Vercel.
Why it's a defect: R1 says every page the app renders loads the container exactly once, "including the 404 page". QA1 ruled that the bare 500 error shell was acceptable. Its premise, that the dataLayer-first rule "holds on every page the layout server-renders, which is every page R1 names", doesn't hold for these notFound() pages: here the layout's tag is not server-rendered into the head.
Impact: every bad date or reading-id URL a visitor opens is missing from GA4, and it costs an extra container fetch. No double-counted hit was observed (0 hits).
Repro: open https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/date/not-a-date with DevTools' Network panel filtered to "gtm.js": 2 requests. Filter to "collect": none.

STEP 1, /date/1969-07-20: PASS.
- gtm.js?id=GTM-T9WQSKH3 loads once (200, initiator parser, from the page HTML).
- The server HTML holds the inline dataLayer snippet in <head>, before the container script, which is async.
- There is no gtag/js script and no G- tag in the page.
- Across a whole visit of five navigations, there was 1 gtm.js load in total.

STEP 2: PASS. Array.isArray(window.dataLayer) is true, and google_tag_manager has key "GTM-T9WQSKH3". dataLayer events: js, gtm.dom, gtm.load.

STEP 3, a GA4 hit on load: PASS.
- POST www.google-analytics.com/g/collect with tid=G-NFY3Q9KSXH, en=page_view, dl=/date/1969-07-20, response 204.
- Each flush also posts to www.google.com/g/collect with the same tid. That's Google's own secondary endpoint (Google signals), not a second tag in this code.

STEP 4, in-app navigation: PAGE VIEWS ARE SENT. The container's history-change setup works.
I followed Next reading to /date/1969-09-01, Previous reading back to /date/1969-07-20, the notable link to /date/1912-04-15, and the banner home link to /date/2026-11-24:
- each navigation added a gtm.historyChange-v2 event to dataLayer (1, 2, 3, 4);
- each produced a page_view with that page's dl: /date/1969-09-01, /date/1969-07-20, /date/1912-04-15 and /date/2026-11-24;
- GA4 batches its hits, so each one goes out at the next navigation, and the last one when the page is left;
- there was no reload, and 1 gtm.js load in total.

STEP 5, other pages:
- /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d: PASS. 200, gtm.js once, page_view sent.
- /no-such-page (404 from an unknown path): PASS. gtm.js once, the snippet in <head>, page_view@/no-such-page.
- Route-level 404s: FAIL, see DEFECT.
- /chart: 307 to /, which goes on to today's date page, so it's covered by the date page result.

STEP 6, absent outside production: PASS. Local build of 2a74097, server HTML read with curl (no JS run, so no hits sent), with dummy Supabase and OpenAI env:
- VERCEL_ENV unset (port 3946): /date/1969-07-20, /no-such-page and /date/not-a-date each have 0 GTM-T9WQSKH3, 0 googletagmanager and 0 dataLayer.
- VERCEL_ENV=preview (port 3947): 0 of each on all three pages.
- VERCEL_ENV=production (port 3948), as a positive control: /date/1969-07-20 has 2 of each, which proves the switch. /date/not-a-date has 1, the defect's pattern. /no-such-page has 0, because the default 404 is prerendered at build time, and this build ran without VERCEL_ENV. On Vercel, production builds with it, which is consistent with step 5.
I didn't look for a Vercel preview deployment.
Servers stopped, clone deleted.

STEP 7, GA4 Realtime: NOT CHECKED. Nobody watched Realtime during the test. The hits above went to G-NFY3Q9KSXH with 204 responses.

Console: the only errors were the expected 404 resource errors on the 404 pages.

PASS: PASS, live-loop audit of f3b47be (fix for LiveQA round 1 CONDITIONAL, against R1). Not a fresh gate-1 pass and not a substitute for LiveQA's retest.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. Unchanged since my gate-1 PASS (last touched at the plan and start commits).

Handoff: read at the audited commit. A Round 2 section was added; Round 1 is untouched (72 insertions, 0 deletions). It quotes VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0, with 513 tests. It states plainly that its Round 1 premise, which my ruling relied on, was wrong.

My own check: npm run verify at f3b47be, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS exit=0, 45 test files and 513 tests passed.

Diff 2a74097..f3b47be in app, lib and README: app/TagManager.tsx, lib/analytics/tag-manager.ts and both test files. layout.tsx, the README and the R3 switch are unchanged.

The fix, checked against the defect LiveQA recorded:
- TagManager now renders one next/script, id gtm, afterInteractive, inline, with no src.
- Its body, GTM_LOADER_SCRIPT, is GTM_INIT_SCRIPT verbatim (unchanged and still pinned by a test). It then creates an async script for GTM_SCRIPT_URL and appends it to head, unless a script with that src is already present.
- This addresses both causes Dev Team identified in next/script:
  (1) a beforeInteractive inline script is inert where the layout renders only in the browser;
  (2) a src script adds a ReactDOM.preload whose fetch wasn't reused, causing the double fetch.
- With no src prop there is no preload. An afterInteractive inline script runs through the client loader whether or not the layout was server-rendered.
- The order is now explicit in code: dataLayer and the js command exist before the container element does. The container is still async.

Dev Team's R2 question: ACCEPTABLE. A script element inserted by the inline half is still Google's snippet in substance. Every invariant R2 actually states holds: dataLayer exists before the container runs, the container loads async through next/script, and there is no second Google tag and no gtag/js tag. This is also the standard GTM loader pattern. Not routing it to Master Controller; R2's own bullets are met.

Tests: meaningful.
- The component test pins exactly one afterInteractive script with no src.
- The new loader test runs the script twice against a fake window and document. It asserts exactly one async container appended, with the exact URL, and that dataLayer already held the js command at the moment of append. That catches both the double-insert and the ordering regression.

Acceptance greps, re-run: GTM-T9WQSKH3 appears once outside tests, at tag-manager.ts:7 (exit 0). The G-/gtag/js pattern matches only the test comment at tag-manager.test.ts:22 (exit 0). NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV is absent (exit 1).

Evidence I read:
- round2-production-build-report.json: each route-level 404 now has gtmScriptRequests 1, with dataLayerFirst holding the js command, and a blocked page_view.
- round2-error-page-report.json: the 500 shell shows 1 request, dataLayer first, and a page_view.
- round2-non-production-builds.txt: 18 grep exit=1 lines.

Nit, in the handoff only: the 500-shell paragraph says the limitation is gone, then its next sentence describes Round 1's behaviour without saying so. It reads as contradictory. The JSON report is unambiguous (1 request), so this is not a blocker.

For LiveQA round 2:
- Re-run the round 1 repro on production: /date/not-a-date, /date/1054-07-04 and the unknown reading id should each show 1 gtm.js request and a page_view.
- Re-check that normal pages, client navigation (1 gtm.js load per visit), and /no-such-page didn't regress.
- Re-check that the tag is absent outside production.

My gate-1 ruling on the error shell rested on a premise LiveQA disproved; I am correcting that record separately with sprint-correct.

No issues found. No new Human Prerequisites. | commit=f3b47be50db72b4ad1dff9ab5fb92727034c1cf8

There the container was fetched twice and no page_view was sent. I accepted Dev Team's premise without testing it against a route-level 404. The verdict itself is superseded by the fix at f3b47be, which I audited as a live-loop PASS (event 5).

Tools:

ROUND 1 DEFECT, route-level 404s: FIXED. Fresh context per page:
- /date/not-a-date: 404, title "404: This page could not be found.", gtm.js loads=1, dataLayer[0] is ["js", <timestamp>], page_view@/date/not-a-date sent.
- /date/1054-07-04: 404, gtm.js loads=1, dataLayer[0] js, page_view@/date/1054-07-04.

NO REGRESSIONS:

Total gtm.js loads for the visit: 1.
- Each hard load of a new document loads gtm.js once (one per document).
- Console: only the expected 404 resource errors on 404 pages, plus a CSS-preload-unused warning on /date/not-a-date.
Design note, not a defect: the inline snippet now runs as an afterInteractive script in body and inserts the container itself, so the inline script is no longer in head before the container. Ordering still holds at runtime: dataLayer[0] is the js command on every page tested. QA1 ruled this acceptable under R2.

- VERCEL_ENV unset (port 3956): /date/1969-07-20, /date/not-a-date, /date/1054-07-04 and /no-such-page each have 0 GTM-T9WQSKH3, 0 googletagmanager and 0 dataLayer.
